prompt:
Create ONE transparent RGBA PNG atlas of three small 2D ground-surface DETAIL overlays, not complete ground textures. Exact target canvas 1536 x 1024 pixels, 2 columns x 2 rows, each cell exactly 768 x 512. No gutters, no labels, no checkerboard artwork, no frames. The bottom-right cell must remain fully transparent. Keep all visible output within its assigned cell. This is one common density-8 canvas: every active cell corresponds to the same 96 x 64 source-world rectangle. Do not resize or rotate individual details to fill their cells.

Reference 1 is an exact source-layout guide. Its three complete original 96 x 64 tiles were enlarged by nearest-neighbor 8x only for placement. They are not the desired new pixel-art appearance. Top-left is G2 diffuse surface variation, top-right G3 short dark surface traces, bottom-left source frame413 short dark surface traces. References 2, 3, and 4 are the same three complete original tiles at native size (G2, G3, frame413), supplied for unambiguous source inspection. Reference 5 is the already-generated HD soil material language. It supplies the material context only: DO NOT reproduce its full soil background in any output cell. The requested output contains only transparent-background detail overlays that can be composited over that existing soil material.

Top-left, G2: make a restrained, irregular, low-contrast diffuse surface-variation overlay corresponding to the broad nonuniform mottled appearance in this source tile. Preserve the approximate source-local arrangement and overall restrained visual mass. Do not redraw its high-frequency source speckle, generate a new full soil tile, invent an object, or add directional lighting/shadows. Keep broad unaffected areas transparent. This is an interpretation of diffuse variation, not recovery of the original layer or alpha. Do not copy the reference bitmap as the detail.

Top-right, G3: retain the small short dark surface traces at their source-local positions, scale, and orientations. The upper-left dark nucleus is around source-local x=5..8, y=4..5, several source pixels below the top edge; do not extend it to the previous tile or invent a continuous line crossing the top boundary. Approximate review areas are source-local [2,0,12,7] and [16,43,37,58]; these are coarse observation boxes, NOT requested rectangular silhouettes and NOT an instruction to fill the boxes. Use the full source tile to keep the marks genuinely small. Render crisp, subtle HD surface detail compatible with the soil reference, with genuine transparent surroundings. No standalone cast shadow, raised object, extra grass, giant scratches, symbols, or recognizable named objects.

Bottom-left, frame413: retain the sparse short dark surface traces in the lower part of its source tile. The main small cluster is approximately source-local [44,46,66,55], retaining its short horizontal grouping, small size, and local placement. This review box is not a filled rectangle or exact silhouette. Do not copy the green grass transition in the original tile; only the short dark surface details are requested. Do not turn all dark soil grain into black marks or make the trace an identifiable crack, footprint, root, or piece of debris. Match the restrained dark marks to the existing HD soil language and leave everything else transparent.

All three cells must use the same absolute source-to-output scale (8 output pixels per source-world pixel), without random rotation, per-cell magnification, decorative arrangement, or moving details toward cell centers. Preserve the empty bottom-right cell. Produce actual transparent alpha, not a colored/white/black background. This result will be judged as three raw candidate overlays; uncertain source meaning must remain understated rather than invented.
